issue.body:
# General

- Nice trick with conditional waiting for `WebComponentsReady`, is that standard practice?
- Like that all mechanisms (`polymer` attribute directive, `@PolymerProperty`,  library selectors) let one choose between not using the capabilities at all, enabling explicitly or enabling implicitly
- Styling is not addressed, right? May be a good idea to keep a list of potential integration issues that the library does not address in the documentation.

# Two-way databinding
- Couldn't `polymer` attribute do event structure translation as well, making `@PolymerProperty` unnecessary? That's what the original angular-polymer does, [here](https://github.com/platosha/angular-polymer/blob/master/src/polymer-element.ts#L129). There are tradeoffs …
- I noticed it uses `nativeElement.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(…))`, where the original angular-polymer used `EventEmitter`. What are the reasons for and implications of the difference?
- `PolymerProperty.unwrap` (and `@PolymerProperty` decorator that uses it) should and does pass through anything that is not `CustomEvent`; may be a good idea to make this clear in the documentation.
- Not 100% sure the names for `polymer` attribute directive and `@PolymerProperty` decorator are perfect, but don't have a better suggestion

# Change Detection
- It was not clear to me (until I looked at the code) that what makes `OnPolymerChange` work is the setter from `@PolymerProperty`; may be a good idea to make this clear in the documentation

# Forms
- Don't yet understand it well enough to comment (though a use of `ironControl` attribute directive to surface the functionality makes sense)

# Polymer Templates
- Good explanation; the actual support (`polymer-template`) is only needed until Angular fixes the flag, right?

issue.title: Deprecate ng-template[polymer] feature
issue.body:
Related to https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/17051

Once `enableLegacyTemplate` is correctly working, `PolymerTemplateDirective` should first check and see if this compiler option is set to false. If it is not, a deprecation warning should be generated.

`PolymerTemplateDirective` ends up doing quite a bit more than the original concept of detaching and reattaching a template. The directive won't be removed entirely. More than likely, it should change to select `ng-template[polymer], template` and automatically apply itself to templates.

Until https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/15557 is fixed, this directive should also attempt to move any children of the template to the template's content property.

issue.body:
I'm working on a project where we integrate web components into a web application using the  preact framework.  For the most part, the issues this site have raised have proven applicable and been very helpful in steering the way we design the application.

One aspect that took me by surprise, though, is that there may be an issue when a custom element uses template tags in the light children area.  In particular, I encountered issues with the Vaadin Grid, which uses inner templates to define the columns.  Something seemed to go wrong in the way the JSX/h engine generated these teplate tags.

It's a little hard to explain what I was seeing.  It was like the template tags weren't quite inert, and the inside of the template turned into strings.  Or something.  I do think there's an issue here.

issue.title: HTML5 template tag has a different behaviour
issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Description When using a regular [template tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/template) inside of a component it doesn't generate a [DocumentFragment](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DocumentFragment) (the content property is empty). From the MDN: > The HTMLTemplateElement has a content property, which is a read-only DocumentFragment containing the DOM subtree which the template represents. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-template-tag In the example you can see in the console the different behavior when running the same code inside of Angular and outside of it. ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** From stackblitz package.json:

issue.title: Renderer breaks HTML Content Templates
issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/compiler. ### Is this a regression? This happens both in Angular 9 and 8. Might be a regression of #1442. ### Description Given the following HTML content template, the `div` node should be part of the content fragment. ```html ``` However, Angular seems to append the `div` node to the `template` node. As a result, the content fragment of the content template is empty, so it's effectively unusable. This breaks compatibility with libraries that need to operate on HTML Content Templates. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/ng-template-fce This repro has two template tags, one in app.component.html (`template#template1`, inside Angular) and one in index.html (`template#template2`, outside Angular). Click _Test template inside Angular_. It shows: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6698344/74958787-c2ed6c80-5409-11ea-9130-f21ad3b13cdc.png) Click _Test template outside Angular_.
